```{r setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(data.table); library(ggplot2); library(knitr) })
ROOT <- normalizePath(file.path(getwd(), "..", ".."))
DOMAIN <- params$domain
OUT <- file.path(ROOT, "03_outputs", "epf_postsoviet", DOMAIN)
Sys.setenv(PISA_DOMAIN = DOMAIN)
source(file.path(ROOT, "02_scripts/epf_postsoviet/00_helpers.R"))
rd_csv <- function(f) { p <- file.path(OUT, f); if (file.exists(p)) fread(p) else NULL }
rd_many <- function(prefix) { fs <- list.files(OUT, pattern = paste0("^", prefix, "_[A-Z]{3}\\.csv$"), full.names = TRUE); if (length(fs)) rbindlist(lapply(fs, fread), fill = TRUE) else NULL }
flow  <- fread(file.path(ROOT, "03_outputs/epf_postsoviet/sample_flow.csv"))
desc  <- rd_csv("desc_systems.csv"); icc <- rd_csv("desc_icc.csv"); icc_c <- rd_csv("mean_icc.csv"); corr <- rd_csv("desc_corr.csv")
bm    <- rd_csv("desc_birthmonth.csv"); sel <- rd_csv("desc_entry_selection.csv")
mm    <- rd_csv("mean_models.csv"); mm_lin <- rd_csv("mean_models_agelinear.csv"); mm_non <- rd_csv("mean_models_agenone.csv")
lq    <- rd_many("lqmm"); med <- rd_many("mediation")
if (!is.null(lq)) { lq[, tau := as.character(tau)]; lq <- unique(lq, by = c("CNT", "model", "tau", "term")) }
sys_order <- c("KAZ", "UZB", "AZE", "GEO", "ARM", "KGZ", "MDA")
lab <- function(x) factor(PS_NAMES[as.character(x)], levels = PS_NAMES[sys_order])
tl  <- function(t) { t <- as.character(t); ifelse(t %in% names(term_lab), term_lab[t], t) }
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom"))
okabe <- c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#999999")
f1 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1); f2 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2)
ci  <- function(e, s) paste0(f1(e), " [", f1(e - 1.96 * s), ", ", f1(e + 1.96 * s), "]")
star <- function(e, s) paste0(f1(e), ifelse(abs(e / s) > 1.96, "*", ""))
# Quantile contrast beta(0.25) - beta(0.75). Outputs produced after 1 Oct carry it with a bootstrap SE (tau == "0.25-0.75");
# older outputs get an approximation that treats the two quantile estimates as independent (conservative, since they are positively correlated).
contrast_exact <- !is.null(lq) && any(lq$tau == "0.25-0.75")
contrasts <- function(dt, model_name, terms) {
  x <- dt[model == model_name & term %in% terms]
  if (contrast_exact) { k <- x[tau == "0.25-0.75", .(CNT, term, diff = est, diff_se = se)] }
  else { w <- dcast(x[tau %in% c("0.25", "0.75")], CNT + term ~ tau, value.var = c("est", "se")); k <- w[, .(CNT, term, diff = est_0.25 - est_0.75, diff_se = sqrt(se_0.25^2 + se_0.75^2))] }
  e <- dcast(x[tau %in% c("0.25", "0.5", "0.75")], CNT + term ~ tau, value.var = "est"); setnames(e, c("0.25", "0.5", "0.75"), c("b25", "b50", "b75"))
  k <- merge(e, k, by = c("CNT", "term")); k[, z := diff / diff_se]
  k[, verdict := fifelse(z > 1.96, "compresses (favours low achievers)", fifelse(z < -1.96, "widens (favours high achievers)", "uniform"))]
  k
}
summ_contrast <- function(k) k[, .(`median β(.25)` = f1(median(b25)), `median β(.75)` = f1(median(b75)), `median contrast` = f1(median(diff)),
                                   `compresses` = sum(verdict %like% "compresses"), `widens` = sum(verdict %like% "widens"), `uniform` = sum(verdict == "uniform"), systems = .N), by = term]
profile_note <- if (!is.null(lq)) paste0(unique(lq$profile), " profile: ", unique(lq$n_pv), " plausible value(s) in lqmm, ", unique(lq$n_boot), " bootstrap draws") else "lqmm outputs not yet available"
```

::: {.callout-note}
**Status.** Domain: **`r dom_lab`**. Quantile mixed models: `r profile_note`. Quantile contrasts: `r if (contrast_exact) "bootstrap SE of the difference" else "approximate SE (independence of the two quantile estimates assumed; exact bootstrap SE produced by the next run of 06_lqmm.R)"`. Mediation outputs: `r if (!is.null(med)) paste(sort(unique(med$CNT)), collapse = ", ") else "not yet run (requires the mediation package)"`. Everything in this report is read from `03_outputs/epf_postsoviet/`; re-run `02_scripts/epf_postsoviet/run_all_estimation.sh` to update.
:::

# Research questions and hypotheses

The paper asks where in the achievement distribution the inputs of the education production function do their work, and whether the socio-emotional skills students bring to school are a channel through which socio-economic disadvantage — their own and their school's — reaches learning. Every question is answered system by system (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Armenia, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova) and summarised by the median across systems; no pooled model is estimated. Grade and birth month enter every model as controls, not as objects of interest.

The organising device is the pair of coefficients an input receives at the 25th and 75th conditional percentiles of the score. Their difference, β(.25) − β(.75), has three readable outcomes: positive means the input raises low achievers more than high achievers and so *compresses* the distribution (a gap-closing input); negative means it *widens* it; zero means it lifts everyone and the gap persists.

| | Research question | Hypothesis | Model | Quantity | Decision rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RQ1 | Does socio-economic disadvantage — the student's own ESCS and the socio-economic composition of the school — bear more heavily on low or on high achievers? | H1: both gradients are at least as large at the 25th as at the 75th percentile (inequality is reproduced along the whole distribution, not only at the top). | lqmm core, τ ∈ {.25, .50, .75}, school random intercept | β_τ for ESCS percentile rank and for LOO school-mean ESCS; contrast β(.25) − β(.75) | contrast > 0 and significant → compresses; < 0 → widens; otherwise uniform |
| RQ2 | Which school inputs that are policy levers — staffing and material shortages, class size, student–teacher ratio, certified teachers, infrastructure, language of instruction, rural location, SEL policy — matter more for low achievers? | H2: shortage and location inputs bite at the bottom of the distribution; composition and language effects are uniform. | lqmm core | β_τ for each school input; contrast | as above, input by input |
| RQ3 | Do socio-emotional skills (Big Five domains) pay off more for low achievers than for high achievers? | H3: task performance and open-mindedness have larger associations at the 25th than at the 75th percentile. | lqmm skills (core + four domain scores), skills sample with IPW | β_τ for task, open-mindedness, adaptability, growth mindset; contrast | as above |
| RQ4 | Is a share of the socio-economic gradient at the 25th percentile transmitted through socio-emotional skills — i.e. are skills a plausible channel for closing the gap? | H4: a non-trivial share (≥ 10 %) of the own-ESCS gradient and of the school-composition gradient at the 25th percentile is mediated by the four skills. The alternative (direct gradient, no skill channel) is the reading in which composition works through the system itself. | Causal mediation (Imai–Keele–Tingley, `mediation`), outcome model = quantile regression at τ = .25; mean model as comparison | ACME, ADE, total effect, mediated share, per exposure and mediator; joint four-skill block | mediated share with its interval; ≥ 10 % counted as substantial |

Two descriptive elements frame the results: the share of achievement variance between schools (ICC) per system, and the conditional grade gradient — the achievement difference between students of the same birth month in adjacent grades — which is reported in the appendix and is not interpreted as a learning gain.

# Data and sample

PISA 2025 public-use files for the seven systems. Every sampled student was born in 2009, so age varies only by birth month and the age controls are twelve birth-month indicators. The estimation sample is students in general programmes (ISCED 244/344) in the modal grade or one grade either side, with ESCS, birth month, sex and school covariates observed; vocational programmes at age 15 (Kazakhstan 13 %, Moldova 7 %, Kyrgyzstan 2 %) are excluded. The skills sample additionally requires all socio-emotional scales and the growth-mindset item and is re-weighted by inverse-probability weights for questionnaire completion (Armenia loses 73 % of students at this step and is kept with that caveat).

```{r tbl-flow}
fl <- dcast(flow, step ~ CNT, value.var = "n"); setcolorder(fl, c("step", sys_order))
fl[, step := factor(step, levels = unique(flow$step))]; setorder(fl, step)
kable(fl, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), caption = "Sample flow by system (students)")
```

```{r tbl-desc}
if (!is.null(desc)) {
  d <- desc[, .(System = PS_NAMES[CNT], Students = n, Schools = schools, `Modal grade` = modal_grade, `Mean score (SE)` = paste0(f1(est_score), " (", f1(se_score), ")"), SD = f1(est_sd),
                `Below Level 2 (%)` = round(100 * est_below_L2), `ESCS mean` = f2(ESCS), `Russian-medium (%)` = round(100 * rus_medium), `Rural (%)` = round(100 * rural), `Skills sample` = skills_n)]
  d <- d[match(PS_NAMES[sys_order], System)][!is.na(System)]
  kable(d, caption = paste0("System descriptives, ", dom_lab, " (weighted; BRR + PV standard errors)"))
}
```

```{r fig-icc, fig.height=4, fig.cap="Share of score variance between schools: unconditional (null model) and conditional on the core covariates."}

  ic <- merge(icc, icc_c, by = "CNT", all.x = TRUE)
  im <- melt(ic[, .(System = lab(CNT), Unconditional = icc, `Conditional (core model)` = icc_conditional)], id.vars = "System")
  ggplot(im, aes(x = value, y = System, colour = variable)) + geom_point(size = 3) + scale_colour_manual(values = okabe[1:2], name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, NA)) + labs(x = "ICC (school level)", y = NULL)

# Models and code

The scripts live in `02_scripts/epf_postsoviet/`; the chunks below show the estimation code that answers each question (not evaluated here — the report reads the CSVs the scripts write).

## Common specification (RQ1–RQ3): linear quantile mixed model

One model per system, school random intercept, three quantiles in one call. The score is fitted in hundreds of points because `lqmm`'s C routines overflow on raw PISA points at Kazakhstan's sample size; coefficients are rescaled afterwards. `lqmm` takes cluster-level weights, so the school mean of the final student weight (normalised) is used, with the inverse-probability weight folded in for the skills model.

```{r code-lqmm, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# 06_lqmm.R (excerpt) — one system, both model sets
student_ctrl <- c("female", "lang_other", "immigrant", "repeated")
hh_ctrl      <- c("ESCS_pct10")                       # within-system percentile rank of ESCS, per 10 points
school_ctrl  <- c("sch_escs_loo", "rural", "private", "clsize", "stratio_med", "proatce",
                  "STAFFSHORT", "EDUSHORT", "infra_poor", "rus_medium", "sel_policy")
skill_dom    <- c("task", "open", "adapt", "growth")  # Big Five domain scores (sample-standardised) + binary growth mindset
rhs_core     <- c("grade_c", "bmonth", student_ctrl, hh_ctrl, school_ctrl)   # grade and birth-month dummies are controls

fit <- lqmm(fixed  = y ~ grade_c + bmonth + female + lang_other + immigrant + repeated + ESCS_pct10 +
                        sch_escs_loo + rural + private + clsize + stratio_med + proatce + STAFFSHORT +
                        EDUSHORT + infra_poor + rus_medium + sel_policy,          # + task + open + adapt + growth in the skills model
            random = ~ 1, group = school, tau = c(.25, .50, .75), nK = 7, type = "normal",
            data = df, weights = df$w_school, control = lqmmControl(LP_max_iter = 2000, UP_max_iter = 50))
b   <- boot(fit, R = NBOOT, seed = 20260930)          # school block bootstrap; array R x term x tau
est <- coef(fit) * 100                                 # back to PISA points
se  <- apply(b[, rownames(coef(fit)), ], c(2, 3), sd, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
# the test of RQ1–RQ3: does the input compress or widen the conditional distribution?
diff_draws <- (b[, , "tau = 0.25"] - b[, , "tau = 0.75"]) * 100
contrast   <- data.table(term = rownames(coef(fit)), est = est[, 1] - est[, 3], se = apply(diff_draws, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE))
# FULL profile: point estimates averaged over 10 plausible values, between-PV variance added (Rubin); bootstrap on PV1.
```

## RQ4: causal mediation at the 25th percentile

Two exposures (own ESCS percentile rank, conditional on school composition; LOO school-mean ESCS, conditional on own ESCS), four mediators one at a time, the joint block as total minus direct. The outcome model is `quantreg::rq` at τ = .25, which `mediation::mediate` accepts; the mediator model is linear (a linear-probability model for the binary growth mindset). Random intercepts are not available inside `mediate`; the leave-one-out school mean is what absorbs sorting into schools.

```{r code-med, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# 10_mediation.R (excerpt) — one system, one exposure, one mediator, quantile outcome model
ctrl <- c("sch_escs_loo", "grade_c", "bmonth", student_ctrl, setdiff(school_ctrl, "sch_escs_loo"))   # when the exposure is ESCS_pct10
f_m  <- task ~ ESCS_pct10 + <ctrl>                                   # mediator model (lm, weights = IPW x student weight)
f_y  <- y    ~ task + ESCS_pct10 + <ctrl>                            # outcome model
mm   <- lm(f_m, data = d, weights = w)
my   <- rq(f_y, tau = 0.25, data = d, weights = w)                   # or lm(...) for the mean comparison
med  <- mediate(mm, my, treat = "ESCS_pct10", mediator = "task", sims = 1000, control.value = 0, treat.value = 1)
c(ACME = med$d0, ADE = med$z0, total = med$tau.coef, share = med$n0)
# joint block: coef on the exposure in rq(y ~ exposure + ctrl) minus coef in rq(y ~ task + open + adapt + growth + exposure + ctrl);
# SE by school-cluster bootstrap. Repeated over PVs 1,3,5,7,9 and Rubin-combined in the FULL profile.
```

## Inference

Mean models (appendix) use all ten plausible values with Fay's BRR replicate weights. Quantile models use the school block bootstrap (`boot.lqmm`) for sampling variance and, in the FULL profile, add the between-PV variance. The quantile contrast's standard error comes from the bootstrap draws of the difference, so the positive correlation between β(.25) and β(.75) is respected; where the saved output predates that addition the report approximates it assuming independence, which is conservative.

# Results

## RQ1 — Socio-economic gradients across the distribution

```{r fig-rq1, fig.cap="Own-ESCS gradient (points per 10 percentile points) and school-composition gradient (points per index unit of LOO school-mean ESCS) at the 25th, 50th and 75th conditional percentiles, by system; 95% CI."}
if (!is.null(lq)) {
  g <- lq[model == "core" & term %in% c("ESCS_pct10", "sch_escs_loo") & tau %in% c("0.25", "0.5", "0.75")]; g[, System := lab(CNT)]; g[, Term := tl(term)]
  ggplot(g, aes(x = tau, y = est, colour = System, group = System)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = est - 1.96 * se, ymax = est + 1.96 * se), position = position_dodge(width = .5), size = .3) + geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = .5), alpha = .5) +
    facet_wrap(~Term, scales = "free_y") + scale_colour_manual(values = okabe, name = NULL) + labs(x = "Conditional quantile", y = paste0(dom_lab, " points"))
}
```

```{r tbl-rq1}
if (!is.null(lq)) {
  k <- contrasts(lq, "core", c("ESCS_pct10", "sch_escs_loo"))
  t1 <- k[, .(System = PS_NAMES[CNT], Input = tl(term), `β(.25)` = f1(b25), `β(.50)` = f1(b50), `β(.75)` = f1(b75), `β(.25) − β(.75)` = star(diff, diff_se), Verdict = verdict)]
  kable(t1[order(Input, match(System, PS_NAMES[sys_order]))], caption = "RQ1: socio-economic gradients by quantile and the quantile contrast (* = |z| > 1.96)")
  kable(summ_contrast(k)[, term := tl(term)], caption = "RQ1 summary across systems: medians and the number of systems in which the input compresses, widens, or acts uniformly")
}
```

```{r fig-rq2, fig.height=9, fig.cap="School-input coefficients at the 25th, 50th and 75th conditional percentiles, by system (points per unit; 95% CI).   ggplot(g, aes(x = est, y = System, colour = tau)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +

    facet_wrap(~Term, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3, labeller = label_wrap_gen(28)) + scale_colour_manual(values = okabe[c(2, 1, 3)], name = "tau") + labs(x = "Coefficient (points)", y = NULL)

```

```{r tbl-rq2}
if (!is.null(lq)) {
  k <- contrasts(lq, "core", setdiff(school_ctrl, "sch_escs_loo"))
  kable(summ_contrast(k)[, term := tl(term)][order(-as.numeric(`median contrast`))], caption = "RQ2 summary across systems: school inputs ordered from most compressing to most widening (median contrast β(.25) − β(.75) in points; counts of systems by verdict)")

  kable(t2, caption = "RQ2 detail: quantile contrast β(.25) − β(.75) by input and system, points (* = |z| > 1.96; positive = favours low achievers)")
}

# Mapping the results to the research questions

```{r tbl-map}
if (!is.null(lq)) {
  k1 <- contrasts(lq, "core", c("ESCS_pct10", "sch_escs_loo")); k2 <- contrasts(lq, "core", setdiff(school_ctrl, "sch_escs_loo"))
  k3 <- if (nrow(lq[model == "skills"]) > 0) contrasts(lq, "skills", skill_dom) else NULL
  line <- function(k, t) { x <- k[term == t]; paste0(tl(t), ": β(.25) ", f1(median(x$b25)), " vs β(.75) ", f1(median(x$b75)), " (median); compresses in ", sum(x$verdict %like% "compresses"), ", widens in ", sum(x$verdict %like% "widens"), ", uniform in ", sum(x$verdict == "uniform"), " of ", nrow(x), " systems") }
  verdict_rq <- function(k, terms, hyp_sign) { x <- k[term %in% terms]; n_c <- sum(x$verdict %like% "compresses"); n_w <- sum(x$verdict %like% "widens"); n_u <- sum(x$verdict == "uniform")
    if (hyp_sign == "compress") { if (n_c > n_w & n_c >= n_u) "Supported: the inputs favour low achievers in most systems" else if (n_u >= n_c & n_u >= n_w) "Not supported in the compressing direction: effects are mostly uniform across the distribution (inputs lift everyone; the gap persists)" else "Rejected: effects are larger for high achievers" }
    else { if (n_w > n_c) "Supported: the gradient is steeper at the top — disadvantage widens the distribution" else if (n_u >= n_c & n_u >= n_w) "Supported in the reproduction sense: the gradient is uniform across the distribution" else "Not supported: the gradient is steeper at the bottom" } }
  rows <- list(
    data.table(RQ = "RQ1", Hypothesis = "H1: own-SES and school-composition gradients at least as large at the bottom as at the top",
               Evidence = paste(line(k1, "ESCS_pct10"), line(k1, "sch_escs_loo"), sep = " / "), Answer = verdict_rq(k1, c("ESCS_pct10", "sch_escs_loo"), "reproduce")),
    data.table(RQ = "RQ2", Hypothesis = "H2: shortage and location inputs bite at the bottom; composition and language uniform",
               Evidence = paste(sapply(c("rural", "STAFFSHORT", "EDUSHORT", "clsize", "stratio_med", "proatce", "infra_poor", "rus_medium", "private", "sel_policy"), function(t) line(k2, t)), collapse = " / "), Answer = verdict_rq(k2, c("rural", "STAFFSHORT", "EDUSHORT", "clsize", "stratio_med", "proatce", "infra_poor"), "compress")))
  if (!is.null(k3)) rows[[3]] <- data.table(RQ = "RQ3", Hypothesis = "H3: task performance and open-mindedness pay off more at the bottom",
               Evidence = paste(sapply(skill_dom, function(t) line(k3, t)), collapse = " / "), Answer = verdict_rq(k3, c("task", "open"), "compress"))
  if (!is.null(med)) { j <- med[mediator == "joint_block" & outcome_model == "q25"]
    rows[[4]] <- data.table(RQ = "RQ4", Hypothesis = "H4: ≥ 10% of the gradient at the 25th percentile is mediated by the four skills",
               Evidence = paste0("Own ESCS: median share ", round(100 * median(j[exposure == "ESCS_pct10", prop])), "% (≥ 10% in ", sum(j[exposure == "ESCS_pct10", prop] >= .1), " of ", nrow(j[exposure == "ESCS_pct10"]), " systems); school-mean ESCS: median share ", round(100 * median(j[exposure == "sch_escs_loo", prop])), "% (≥ 10% in ", sum(j[exposure == "sch_escs_loo", prop] >= .1), " systems)"),
               Answer = fifelse(median(j[exposure == "sch_escs_loo", prop]) >= .1, "Supported: skills are a measurable channel of the composition gradient at the bottom of the distribution", "Not supported for school composition: the composition gradient at the bottom is direct — the Bowles reading")) }
  else rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.table(RQ = "RQ4", Hypothesis = "H4: ≥ 10% of the gradient at the 25th percentile is mediated by the four skills", Evidence = "pending (mediation not yet run)", Answer = "pending")
  kable(rbindlist(rows), caption = "Results mapped to the research questions (medians across systems; verdicts from the quantile contrasts)")
}
```

Power note for the current profile. With 30 bootstrap draws and the independence approximation for the contrast's standard error, the verdicts above are conservative: an input whose medians are −9.6 at the 25th and −1.3 at the 75th percentile (rural location) is classified "uniform" in every system only because the interval of the difference is wide. The medians give the direction; the FULL run (200 draws, exact bootstrap SE of the difference) gives the test. Read the counts as provisional until then.

Reading the map. The decisive comparison for the paper's title question is between RQ1 and RQ2–RQ3: where disadvantage (RQ1) is uniform or widening across the distribution while some inputs (RQ2) or skills (RQ3) are compressing, those inputs are the levers that close the gap; where everything is uniform, the production function lifts all students equally and the gap is structural. RQ4 then says whether the socio-emotional channel is one of those levers or whether the composition gradient bypasses it.

# Appendix

## The conditional grade gradient

The coefficient on grade is the achievement difference between students of the same birth month in adjacent grades, conditional on the covariates. It is a control in the quantile models and is not interpreted as a learning gain: in a single cross-section the student who is a grade ahead at a given age is also the youngest in her class, so schooling and relative-age effects are not separately identified (Avvisati & Givord 2021, 2023).

```{r tbl-grade}
if (!is.null(mm)) {
  g <- mm[term == "grade_c" & model %in% c("M1a_gross", "M1b_core", "M1d_within", "M1e_lmer"), .(CNT, model = c(M1a_gross = "Gross (grade + birth-month dummies)", M1b_core = "Core (+ controls)", M1d_within = "Core + school FE", M1e_lmer = "Core, school random intercept")[model], v = ci(est, se))]
  gw <- dcast(g, CNT ~ model, value.var = "v"); gw[, System := PS_NAMES[CNT]]; gw <- gw[match(sys_order, CNT)][!is.na(CNT)]; gw[, CNT := NULL]; setcolorder(gw, "System")
  kable(gw, caption = paste0("Grade coefficient, ", dom_lab, " points per grade, estimate [95% CI], BRR + PV inference"))
}
if (!is.null(mm) && !is.null(mm_lin) && !is.null(mm_non)) {
  g <- rbind(mm[term == "grade_c" & model == "M1b_core", .(CNT, age = "Birth-month dummies", v = ci(est, se))], mm_lin[term == "grade_c" & model == "M1b_core", .(CNT, age = "Linear age (months)", v = ci(est, se))], mm_non[term == "grade_c" & model == "M1b_core", .(CNT, age = "No age term", v = ci(est, se))])
  gw <- dcast(g, CNT ~ age, value.var = "v"); gw[, System := PS_NAMES[CNT]]; gw <- gw[match(sys_order, CNT)][!is.na(CNT)]; gw[, CNT := NULL]; setcolorder(gw, c("System", "No age term", "Linear age (months)", "Birth-month dummies"))
  kable(gw, caption = "Sensitivity of the core grade coefficient to the age specification")
}
```

```{r fig-bm, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Grade allocation by birth month (general programmes, modal grade +/- 1): weighted share of students above (blue) and below (orange) the modal grade."}

  ggplot(b, aes(x = bmonth)) + geom_col(aes(y = share_above), fill = okabe[1], alpha = .8, width = .7) + geom_col(aes(y = -share_below), fill = okabe[2], alpha = .8, width = .7) +

## Mean-model coefficients (for continuity with the 2018 design)

```{r tbl-core}
if (!is.null(mm)) {
  g <- mm[model == "M1b_core" & !term %like% "bmonth" & term != "(Intercept)", .(CNT, term, v = star(est, se))]
  gw <- dcast(g, term ~ CNT, value.var = "v"); gw[, Term := tl(term)]; gw[, term := NULL]; setcolorder(gw, c("Term", intersect(sys_order, names(gw))))
  med_ <- mm[model == "M1b_core" & !term %like% "bmonth" & term != "(Intercept)", .(Median = f1(median(est))), by = term]; gw <- merge(gw, med_[, .(Term = tl(term), Median)], by = "Term", sort = FALSE)
  gw <- gw[order(match(Term, tl(c("grade_c", student_ctrl, hh_ctrl, school_ctrl))))]
  kable(gw, caption = "Core mean model (M1b) coefficients by system, points; * = |t| > 1.96 (BRR + PV). Last column: median across systems.")
}
if (!is.null(mm)) {
  g <- mm[model == "M1c_skills" & term %in% skill_dom, .(System = PS_NAMES[CNT], Skill = tl(term), v = ci(est, se))]
  kable(dcast(g, Skill ~ System, value.var = "v"), caption = "Skill coefficients in the mean model (M1c, skills sample, IPW): points per SD of the domain score, 95% CI")
}

## Diagnostics and notes

```{r tbl-skillsmiss}
if (!is.null(mm)) {
  g <- mm[model %in% c("M1b_core", "M1c_core_on_skills_sample") & term %in% c("grade_c", "ESCS_pct10", "sch_escs_loo"), .(CNT, model = fifelse(model == "M1b_core", "core sample", "skills sample (IPW)"), term = tl(term), v = f1(est))]
  kable(dcast(g, CNT + term ~ model, value.var = "v"), caption = "Sensitivity of key coefficients to the skills-sample restriction (core specification on both samples)")
}
if (!is.null(sel)) kable(sel[, .(System = PS_NAMES[CNT], `ESCS gap: above-modal vs modal (within birth month)` = f2(escs_gap_above), `ESCS gap: below-modal vs modal (within birth month)` = f2(escs_gap_below))], caption = "Selection into early and late school entry: within-birth-month ESCS differences between students outside and inside the modal grade (index units)")
```

- **Weights in lqmm.** `lqmm` accepts cluster-level weights only; the school mean of the final student weight (normalised) is used, with the IPW folded in for the skills model. Mean models use the full replicate-weight design.
- **Units.** PROATCE is released in the 2025 PUF as a 1–5 category and STRATIO as international quartiles (medians used); both are labelled accordingly.
- **Profile.** `r profile_note`. The FULL profile (10 PVs, 200 bootstrap draws, exact quantile-contrast SEs, mediation with 1,000 simulations) is run with `PISA_PROFILE=FULL 02_scripts/epf_postsoviet/run_all_estimation.sh` and overwrites the same CSVs.
